en: A moth the size of a gull, drawn to Lanternfall's lights. The ember eyespots on its soot-grey wings read like a leaf-boat's flame in the dark, and the dust off them brings sleep.
A low tortoise under a shell of cooled lava flecked with copper. It pulls in when struck, and ordinary blows glance off. Something heavy has to crack it first.
A lean copper-green lizard that sleeps on the Lit Age veins and stores their charge. It carries its tail curled up like a coil, and it spits lightning.

A forge-keeper from when Ashcrown's copper was a working line, crusted in centuries of slag. The Tenders tend her like an old relative. She wakes when the anvil rings, and she tests the Cantor's guardians, never the Cantor.
Armoured foes turn ordinary blows aside. Kerrid's Fluke Cleave breaks their armour for a while: watch the timeline for how long.
The Matron's crust turns blows aside. Kerrid can break it.
Water and cold will harden her again.
A massive hooked blade forged from a ship's anchor fluke, carried bare across the back.
Cloth wound tight from wrist to elbow, old and many times retied.
An iron charm from Ashcrown's quench-trough. A smith dips it in the trough before a big piece of work, for luck against the fire.
A Pemakar leaf-boat, folded and unlit, with a pinch of rice in it. Carried until it is time.
